{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOQ7BKhc8AAAABXX4YCg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm6sGzhA7-O8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm6sG", "number": 21, "title": "Support dynamic material and model reference TSL nodes", "body": "## Problem

Draft v2.0 now supports many ordinary TSL expression, texture and shading nodes, but the default loader/exporter still rejects **ordinary instances** of several useful dynamic material/model reference nodes. The exact shared `three/tsl` exports (e.g. `materialColor`, `modelPosition`) already resolve by identity; this issue targets additional instances and their correctly preserved runtime behavior.

Support the next four agreed classes where doing so is safe and maintainable:

1. `MaterialNode`
2. `ModelNode`
3. `MaterialReferenceNode`
4. `Object3DNode`

The primary goal is to reconstruct **live references**, not snapshot referenced properties into literals or serialize JavaScript object graphs.

## Expected outcome

- Add paired **default serializer and resolver** handling to the existing exporter and loader plugins for safe, well-defined variants of the four classes, using the actual Three.js **r186** implementations as a baseline; recheck the latest stable version at implementation time.
- Preserve class-specific scope/property identifiers, supported types, optional values and graph relationships. Reuse Three.js classes and `serialize()`/`deserialize()`/`getSerializeChildren()` when appropriate, rather than duplicating node/runtime semantics.
- `MaterialNode`: preserve supported scope selection and dynamic access to the current material, including properties also imported from ordinary glTF PBR and supported material extensions.
- `ModelNode`: preserve supported model scopes using Three.js's current-rendered-object semantics; the imported node must follow transform changes, not the original transform value.
- `MaterialReferenceNode`: support a deliberately **allowlisted**, type-checked set of ordinary material properties when they can be rebound to the **current rendered material** (no embedded foreign material objects). Preserve runtime updates after import and clarify how references behave for shared materials and GLTFLoader-generated clones.
- `Object3DNode`: support only scopes and bindings for which the importer can correctly reconstruct the *intended* object reference in Three.js. Audit the r186 constructor/update implementation: do not assume `object3d: null` automatically binds the current mesh. If a current-mesh binding requires a small explicit adapter/hook, implement it only if clear and maintainable; otherwise defer that variant with a precise explanation. No silent retargeting to a different object.
- For explicit external materials/objects, arbitrary property names, object identities that cannot be expressed through the current graph/glTF structure, dangerous properties, or unresolved object lifetime semantics: **reject or defer rather than guessing**. Document exactly which variants need a consumer-provided adapter/binding and why.
- Continue to protect shared TSL singleton instances from file-supplied mutations. Never evaluate file-provided code or instantiate arbitrary constructors from file-controlled names.
- Preserve Draft v2.0 full-extension fallback per material on invalid identifiers, unsupported scopes/property types, broken links, failed bindings, or invalid graphs. No partial TSL application.

## Context and reproduction

- [Current coverage inventory](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/docs/tsl-node-coverage.md) — live object/material references currently require explicit adapters.
- [Exporter default serializer](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/exporter/src/defaultNodeSerializer.ts)
- [Loader default resolver](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/blob/main/packages/loader/src/defaultNodeResolver.ts)
- [Existing real loader/exporter tests](https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/tree/main/packages/demo/test)
- [Three.js r186 MaterialNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/MaterialNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 ModelNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/ModelNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 MaterialReferenceNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/MaterialReferenceNode.js)
- [Three.js r186 Object3DNode](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/r186/src/nodes/accessors/Object3DNode.js)
- Related implemented nodes: #15, #17, #19.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Audit all four class implementations and enumerate supported/deferred modes, required runtime bindings and class-specific fields.
- [ ] Implement paired serializer/resolver handling for each **feasible** class/variant without unnecessary complexity. Explain any deferred `Object3DNode` binding or other unsupported mode explicitly; do not fake generic support.
- [ ] Add real `GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader → GLTFExporter → GLTFLoader` tests for each supported class, including shared nodes/materials, material clones, dynamically changing material properties and object transforms.
- [ ] Check reconstructed graph structure and, where practical, actual Three.js shader-generation/runtime update behavior (not just exported JSON equality).
- [ ] Test unsupported external object bindings, malformed scopes/property/type data and broken references: exporter must not silently serialize a different meaning, and loader must atomically retain ordinary glTF fallback.
- [ ] Update `docs/tsl-node-coverage.md` and both plugin READMEs with exact supported scopes/allowlists, nonportable cases and explicit adapter paths.
- [ ] Keep the Draft v2.0 specification unchanged, v1.0 support removed, and Three.js-first/minimal-implementation principles intact.
- [ ] Run full integration tests, loader/exporter/demo builds, demo typecheck, and `git diff --check`. Report executed checks and optional skips.

## Optional validation

Browser/WebGPU visual checks of live material/transform updates if suitable infrastructure is available; if skipped, document the limitation of Node-based tests.

## Required post-merge verification

None. **Do not publish npm packages**; the maintainer will publish manually in a separate release step.", "url": "https://github.com/takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl/issues/21", "created_at": "2026-10-15T09:23:23Z", "state": "OPEN", "repository": "takahirox/THREE_materials_tsl", "labels": ["task"], "priority": null, "status": "In Progress", "is_archived": false}, "context": {}, "resources": {}, "allocation": {}, "instruction": null, "run_id": "b46646699c0942ba95ac8bbf073bf1fd"}
